attribution.note: Marcus's own authorial assertion in his Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase of a retrospective claim that Murati's non-answer fits a longstanding OpenAI pattern.

contract.note: The plain reading (repeated evasive or misleading communication before Sora) is ordinary and fair. 'Evasion' and 'longstanding' are undefined, so the result depends on interpretation, as the contract says.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous reporting of Altman in 2016 choosing not to correct a misconception about openness. This is one earlier instance.
Establishes the Sora non-answer that prompted the claim. It says nothing about earlier conduct.
OpenAI's own announcement disclosed the Kociemba solver. This weakens the cube example but does not rebut the broader pattern.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes the Sora non-answer and one earlier instance (2016). It does not establish repeated earlier evasions over several years, which the support condition requires. The cube example is weakened, but nothing substantively rebuts the alleged pattern. Neither condition is met.

attribution.note: The narrator aside is Marcus's own assertion. Brockman's quoted email is not the claim.

semantics.note: The scored part is the retrospective 'they never have'. The rhetorical 'never, ever' is rightly not treated as a forecast. target_version GPT-3 is narrower than 'any of our software', but the proposition keeps the universal scope.

contract.note: Fair reading: no advance red-team access for Marcus through the post date. It rightly excludes Marcus's own statements as proof.

evidence.note: Reports that Marcus lacked GPT-3 API access in August 2020. This is one early point in time, not the full history through 2024.
Shows OpenAI's red-teaming program existed. Nothing in it is specific to Marcus.

reviews.rationale: No complete access history and no independent record either confirms or refutes that Marcus ever got advance red-team access through March 15, 2024. The 2020 lack of API access is a single early point. The evidence does not settle the universal claim.

attribution.note: The 'Translation' is Marcus's own interpretive assertion, citing emails and meetings by Sutskever and Altman.

semantics.note: Faithfully captures the attributed intent: a recruiting promise, not meant to be kept, with the public misconception left uncorrected.

contract.note: Requiring evidence of insincere intent matches Marcus's words ('don't intend to live up to'). Whether near-term sharing followed by later restriction counts as insincerity is an interpretive choice that decides the result.

evidence.note: The pledge's actual wording encourages publication and patent sharing. It does not promise to release everything.
Sutskever's January 2016 email ties sharing to recruitment and expects less openness later. It also endorses real near-term sharing, which cuts against total insincerity.
Altman in May 2016 declined to correct a broad belief about releasing source code. This supports the 'shouldn't disabuse' part.

reviews.rationale: Two parts have support: recruitment as a motive (e5) and leaving the misconception uncorrected (e6). The core claim, that leaders did not intend to honor the 2015 commitments, is not established, since e5 also backs genuine near-term sharing. Nothing contradicts the claim either, so the evidence does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own technical gloss on OpenAI's 2019 announcement.

semantics.note: Revision 2 correctly removes the 'overstated' verdict and the exclusivity claim, leaving Marcus's factual description.

contract.note: Fair not to read 'only' into the wording. Under that reading, the vision-only variant does not contradict the claim.

evidence.note: The announcement says the networks carry out face rotations generated by Kociemba's algorithm. This confirms an existing solver plus learned manipulation.
The paper describes a modified Giiker cube with internal encoders and Bluetooth, used in some experiments. It also reports vision-only work.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own documents from the time show that Kociemba's existing algorithm chose the moves, the learned policy handled manipulation, and a customized cube with internal sensors and Bluetooth was used. The vision-only variant does not contradict wording that does not claim exclusivity.
